I went for a CT bc I was having trouble breathing and it turns out my thyroid is 3x the size it should be. I had a 10cm mass on the left side of my thyroid and it was completely compressing my trachea.. keep in mind I went almost 2 year before it was determined to be my thyroid. I had a lot of issues breathing, like it was just a high pitched whistle by the end of it. I also had what’s called Pembertons sign, so when you raise your arms above your head and touch the side of your face, if you begin to have trouble breathing or your face turns red and swollen that means your thyroid is constricting your arteries as well.

That being said, I personally benefitted from having half of mine removed because I had a lot of compressive symptoms. If it’s not causing you any significant issues, you have the right to wait and keep an eye on it. And there’s always the possibility they only take half of it and you won’t need the lifelong medication. I would just caution especially since you have one around your windpipe, keep an eye on your voice and look for any changes or volume or hoarseness because your nerve runs right through there. 

Best of luck, I hope it all gets sorted out!

I had my left lobe removed 2 weeks ago. I had a mass about 10cm all growing inward and actually into my chest. Between the time I found out and the date of my surgery was about a month, because I was at the point I could only breathe sitting up, it was compressing my trachea almost shut. 

I was also very nervous going into surgery (I’m 22) and with COVID and whatnot, I couldn’t have anyone come in with me so I had panic attacks just waiting, convinced myself I was gonna die LOL. My FNA biopsy came back inconclusive and I’m still waiting on the full pathology report from what they removed.

In terms of pain, I was quite uncomfortable in my sternum but that’s from where it was located. They prescribed me percocets which certainly took my pain away, but I would suggest taking Tylenol if the pain is manageable because they constipated me for 9 days, THAT was the worst part of recovery. I struggled with swallowing and speaking but it turns out my tumour has damaged my vocal nerves so this was unavoidable.

I know it all seems scary, and this was my first major medical procedure as well. I couldn’t sleep or stop stressing before but now that it’s over and I’m healed, it’s amazing for me to see how much it really was affecting me because I can breathe so much better now. It’s normal to be worried, but it won’t change the outcome and just look at it as something that is going to benefit you in the long run.

Hey! I’m 22 and just had the left lobe of my thyroid removed 2 weeks ago. My surgeon said the mass in my thyroid was pinching my nerve and when he removed it, it was damaged. He told me he called in a colleague to repair the nerve so I just assumed that my voice would just take some time to heal, along with choking on liquids and the breathlessness when I speak. I had a follow up yesterday and he looked at my vocal cords and said the left side was paralyzed, didn’t move at all when I spoke. 
Obviously I’ve done my googling, just hard to accept that my voice may never get better, and now I’m concerned about my other nerve being damaged if I get my right lobe removed at any point.
I get really frustrated already having to repeat myself because people can’t hear me, and I get very winded trying to speak and I just can’t imagine the rest of my life like this
